blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, taxable income is not a number the accounting team simply produces — it is a lever shaped by structural choices. Which entity recognises which revenue? Where are costs booked? Which group company owns which asset? How are management fees allocated between jurisdictions? Each question moves the boundary of what is taxable where, and each movement carries legal and reputational consequences the leader has to weigh honestly.

What makes this difficult is the line between planning that is sound and planning that is aggressive. Sound planning uses structures the law intends. Aggressive planning uses structures the law permits but would prefer you did not exploit. Both are legal. The difference appears only in the long run, when the aggressive company's reputation becomes the case study nobody wants to be in.

Responsible senior leaders stay firmly on the sound side of that line — not out of fear, but because the quiet reputation of steady, defensible numbers is worth more than any single saving.

items.q: According to the text, what is taxable income at senior level?
options: The same thing as accounting profit
A lever shaped by structural choices
A fixed figure the accounting team produces
A number set by the tax authority
items.why: "it is a lever shaped by structural choices" — não é um número que a contabilidade apenas gera.

items.q: What distinguishes aggressive planning from sound planning, according to the text?
options: Aggressive planning is illegal, sound planning is legal
Both are legal, but aggressive planning uses structures the law would prefer you did not exploit
Aggressive planning is cheaper in the long run
items.why: "Both are legal" — a diferença é que o agressivo usa estruturas que a lei permite mas preferiria que você não explorasse.

items.q: When does the difference between sound and aggressive planning become visible?
options: Only in the long run, through reputation
items.why: "The difference appears only in the long run… the case study nobody wants to be in."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Structural choices move the boundary of what is taxable
If a structure is legal, that alone settles whether a leader should use it
Reputation can outweigh a short-term tax saving
Sound planning uses structures the law intends
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que legalidade não basta — reputação e o "intended vs permitted" também pesam.

items.q: The phrase "not out of fear" suggests that responsible leaders stay on the sound side because…
options: they are afraid of being caught by regulators
their accountants refuse to sign off
they judge a steady reputation to be more valuable than the saving
items.why: Inferência: "not out of fear, but because the quiet reputation… is worth more than any single saving" — é escolha de valor, não medo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte na reunião sobre a proposta de estrutura intercompany. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks — and I want to be clear, I'm not questioning whether this is legal. The advisers have confirmed it is, and I take that at face value. What I'm questioning is whether it's the kind of structure we want our name attached to.

The proposal shifts a large share of the management fee into the lower-tax entity, and reallocates where the hedging gains are recognised. On paper the saving is significant. But read it back to yourself as if it were a headline. That's the test I keep applying, and this one doesn't pass it comfortably.

My worry is the boundary. We would be sitting right on the line the law permits but plainly did not intend. If a regulator, or a journalist, ever asked us to explain the commercial logic, I'm not sure we could — beyond the tax outcome itself. And when your only justification is the tax, that's usually the tell.

So I'm asking us to hold off. Let's take the sound version of this — smaller saving, but a number we could defend in any room, to anyone, without flinching. I'd rather bank a quieter figure than spend three years explaining a clever one.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Charlotte say she is NOT questioning?
items.why: "I'm not questioning whether this is legal… I take that at face value."

items.q: What test does Charlotte say she keeps applying to the proposal?
options: Whether the auditors have approved it
Whether it would read well as a headline
items.why: "read it back to yourself as if it were a headline. That's the test I keep applying."

items.q: What does the proposal do with the management fee and the hedging gains?
options: Splits both equally across all entities
Leaves them unchanged but documents them better
Shifts the fee to the lower-tax entity and reallocates where the gains are recognised
Removes the fee and defers all gains
items.why: "shifts a large share of the management fee into the lower-tax entity, and reallocates where the hedging gains are recognised."

items.q: When Charlotte says "when your only justification is the tax, that's usually the tell," she implies that…
options: regulators only care about the tax rate
the tax saving proves the structure is sound
the commercial logic is always obvious
a structure with no commercial rationale beyond tax is a warning sign
items.why: Inferência: 'the tell' = o sinal de alerta; sem lógica comercial além do imposto, a estrutura é suspeita.

items.q: How would you best describe Charlotte's position?
options: She is indifferent and defers to the advisers
She prefers a smaller, defensible saving over a larger, hard-to-explain one
She accepts it because the saving is large
She rejects the deal because it is illegal
items.why: Inferência: "I'd rather bank a quieter figure than spend three years explaining a clever one."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Where costs are booked is a structural choice, not an accident." A structural choice is…
options: a deliberate decision about how the organisation is arranged
items.why: Structural choice = escolha estrutural: uma decisão deliberada sobre como a empresa se organiza.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The entity may only ___ revenue once control of the goods has passed to the buyer."
items.why: To recognise revenue = reconhecer receita: registrá-la quando as condições contábeis são cumpridas.

items.q: A management fee is best described as…
options: a charge one group company makes to another for services or oversight
a fine imposed by the tax authority
the salary of the finance director
items.why: Management fee = taxa de gestão cobrada entre empresas do grupo por serviços/supervisão.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The dispute was over how to ___ the shared costs fairly between the two jurisdictions."
items.why: To allocate = alocar: distribuir custos entre entidades ou jurisdições.

items.q: "The plan pushed the company right up to the boundary of what the law intended." A boundary here is…
options: the dividing line between acceptable and unacceptable
items.why: Boundary = fronteira: a linha que separa o sólido do agressivo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre planejamento e estrutura. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the intercompany structure." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Charlotte pushed back on the proposal." She…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Let's not lose sight of the reputational cost." To lose sight of something means to…
items.why: Lose sight of = perder de vista, deixar de considerar algo importante.

items.q: "A smaller saving we can stand behind beats a larger one we can't." To stand behind something means to…
items.why: Stand behind = respaldar, defender publicamente algo em que se acredita.

items.q: "On its own, the tax outcome doesn't hold up as a rationale." To hold up here means to…
items.why: Hold up = resistir ao exame; um argumento que 'holds up' se sustenta sob análise.
